messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: how to concatenate strings?
parts:
I'm wondering if anyone knows a better way to concatenate strings
than how I did it first in C++ using string streams.

We have a lot of uses in our error-handling code that now
looks like this:

```
std::ostringstream msg;
msg << "is not a valid correlation matrix. "
<< name << "(" << stan::error_index::value + k
<< "," << stan::error_index::value + k
<< ") is "; ;
std::string msg_str(msg.str());
dom_err(function, name, y(k,k),
msg_str.c_str(),
", but should be near 1.0");
```

This is using an output string stream to construct a message,
then it creates a std::string to make a copy of the string
contents of the message that will persist through the call to dom_err.
I don't think we do any fancy formatting anywhere, though maybe
we should.

I'd prefer to stick to C++ because there's no potential of
runtime format errors the way you get with printf and cousins.

- Bob

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] how to concatenate strings?
parts:
If it’s just strings then operator+ will concatenate fine —
the problem is the indices which need to be cast to strings
(and why I think the stream was used in the first place).
There are C functions that do the trick (but are considered
bad practice) and really nice C++11 functions that would
solve the problem. If we’re stuck with C++98 then I think
the only options are to use the stream or Boost’s lexical
cast.
